profile.summary: scRM (the single-cell read model) embeds single cells directly from raw sequencing reads, without a reference genome, gene annotation, count matrix or gene vocabulary. It takes paired 10x Chromium polyA FASTQ files, assembles each captured molecule from its reads, and learns a cell embedding from the base sequences; count matrices are used only as evaluation targets.

summary_quotes.text: Cells are embedded directly from **raw sequencing bytes** (A/C/G/T): no reference genome, no gene annotation, no count matrix, no gene vocabulary, no ortholog bridge.
Scope is 10x Chromium single-cell polyA assays
Count matrices are permitted on the **evaluation side only**, as prediction targets

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: A Rust pipeline reads paired FASTQ files, trims R2, corrects cell barcodes against the CellRanger called-cell list, deduplicates UMIs without any gene partition, and assembles one consensus sequence per UMI (one captured mRNA) with a de Bruijn graph at k = 19. The molecules are written to an Arrow corpus sorted by cell and packed into windows of 16384 tokens. The Python model is hierarchical (bytes, contig, UMI, window, cell): a byte-level local transformer trunk, attention pooling at each level, and a global trunk over UMI slots, both LLaMA-style pre-norm stacks. Training combines masked base modelling, EMA-teacher terms at UMI and cell level, and a SIGReg regulariser.

quotes.text: Hamming-1 correction against an **explicit list** of CellRanger-called cells
per cell, with **no gene partition**: there is no reference, so there are no genes
one UMI is one captured mRNA
the hierarchy is **bytes ⊂ contig ⊂ UMI ⊂ window ⊂ cell**

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Three training arms are declared: S96, the flagship with global and local width 96, and S96ML and S96MA, mean-pooling ablations. The flagship recipe is fixed in code (arm S96, the corpora mouse_brain_5k, neuron_1k_v3, neurons_5k and sod1_spinal_cord, lambda 0.0196, seed 20260903, 8947 steps, 3000 training cells). Window length moves only on a ladder of 16384, 32768 and 49152 tokens, and runs at different rungs are different experiments. Checkpoints record the architecture hash and the regulariser. The sources do not offer a pretrained scRM checkpoint for download; the README's evaluation reads a checkpoint produced by training. A result should name the run, the arm, the seq_len rung and the commit.

quotes.text: LAMB=0.0196 REGULARIZER=sigreg SEED=20260903 STEPS=8947 TRAIN_CELLS=3000 TRAIN_FRAC=1.0
Runs at different rungs are different experiments and their curves are not comparable.

sections.title: Intended uses
sections.body: Reference-free cell embeddings from raw reads (the paper's cross-species panels use rhesus monkey and rat corpora for training), scored against count-based controls and count foundation-model baselines on held-out datasets.

quotes.text: embed a checkpoint over ONE held-out dataset and score it against the controls + count-FM panel

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Reference-free single-cell embedding model trained on raw read sequences.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Hierarchical byte-level transformer: local trunk, attention pooling over contigs, UMIs, windows and views, and a global trunk over UMI slots (LLaMA-style pre-norm, RMSNorm, SwiGLU). Flagship width 96.

quotes.text: A byte-level local trunk, then one masked `SegmentAttentionPool` per level

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: Paired gzipped FASTQ from 10x Chromium polyA assays, a samplesheet with an FGDL geometry string and the CellRanger called-cell barcode list.

quotes.text: `geometry` is an FGDL string, not a chemistry name

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: A per-window embedding artifact with a provenance stamp; cell embeddings come from offline window-to-cell reductions (mean, median, max, l2_mean, first).
facts.source_locator: README.md: Architecture item 11; Training, embedding, scoring

quotes.text: the embedding artifact is **per window** and carries a stamp that cannot be omitted
Window→cell reductions are named in every report: `mean`, `median`, `max`, `l2_mean`, `first`.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: Not stated in the sources read.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: The flagship trains on four corpora (mouse_brain_5k, neuron_1k_v3, neurons_5k, sod1_spinal_cord) with 3000 training cells. The paper's scope is twenty corpora.

quotes.text: The paper's scope is twenty corpora.

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: Arms S96 (flagship), S96ML and S96MA; the README and REPRODUCE.md offer no checkpoint download.

quotes.text: There are **three**, and `train.py --help` prints exactly that set

facts.label: Training cutoff
facts.value: Not applicable: the model is trained on fixed public 10x corpora pinned by digest.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: 16384 tokens per window by default (ladder 16384, 32768, 49152); molecules up to 1600 bases (max_umi_len).

facts.value: Unavailable: the README and REPRODUCE.md offer no scRM checkpoint download. Third-party baseline weights are not redistributed.

strengths.text: Needs no reference genome, annotation or gene vocabulary, so the same pipeline applies across species.

quotes.text: no reference genome, no gene annotation, no count matrix, no gene vocabulary, no ortholog bridge

strengths.text: Strong provenance: corpora pinned by digest, stamped artifacts and checks that refuse mismatched inputs.

strengths.text: MIT-licensed code with a scripted reproduction of the paper's numbers (stages 0 to 5 need nothing private).

limitations.text: The README and REPRODUCE.md offer no pretrained weights; users build corpora and train.
Limited to 10x Chromium single-cell polyA assays; Flex and spatial are out of scope.

quotes.text: probe-based (Flex) and spatial are out of scope

limitations.text: Heavy compute and storage: about 350 GB of reads become about 141 GB of corpus for the 20 datasets, and embedding took about 4h50 on 8-9 H100s; workflows assume Slurm.

run_guide.summary: Build scRM from source, build a corpus from paired FASTQ files and train the flagship model; the README and REPRODUCE.md offer no pretrained checkpoint to download.
prerequisites: Rust 1.85 or newer and Python 3.11 or newer.
Paired 10x Chromium polyA FASTQ files, a CellRanger called-cell barcode list and a samplesheet CSV.
A GPU cluster for training; the reproduction scripts assume Slurm.

steps.title: Get the code and build
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/altoslabs/scRM
cd scRM
git checkout --detach 7afa21a788c8c9ee870e697e23e60954fc152c77
pip install -r requirements.txt
cargo build --release
cargo build --release -p scrm-py && mkdir -p target/py \
  && cp target/release/libscrm_py.so target/py/scrm_py.so
steps.explanation: The README's install commands; the clone and checkout lines are added by Rewire to pin the reviewed commit.

steps.title: Build a corpus
steps.explanation: Replace the samplesheet and set SCRM_PROJ to your data root. This is the README's build command with one change: the README example writes to $SCRM_PROJ/corpus_v3, which REPRODUCE.md calls the predecessor root, while the release's corpus root is $SCRM_PROJ/corpus_rel, so --out points there. Each experiment is built into its own folder under --out and manifest.json is written last. The training launcher refuses a corpus that is not in the pinned digest file, so for the flagship the four pretraining corpora must match the pinned digests; REPRODUCE.md builds them with the per-dataset launchers that ./reproduce.sh --dry-run 2 prints, and the saved files do not say whether this direct command reproduces those digests.
steps.source_locator: README.md: Building the corpus; REPRODUCE.md: What this release can reproduce today, From a clean clone to the tables

quotes.text: is the release's corpus root, and it is `reproduce.sh`'s default.
The predecessor root `corpus_v3` is not: its twenty corpora were built before trimming moved into the builder
export SCRM_CORPUS_ROOT=$SCRM_PROJ/corpus_rel      # the release's root; not $SCRM_PROJ/corpus
`--dry-run 2` print the fetch and build launcher for every dataset

steps.title: Train the flagship
steps.shell:
export SCRM_PROJ=/path/to/data-root
export SCRM_PY=/path/to/envs/scrm/bin/python
export SCRM_CORPUS_ROOT=$SCRM_PROJ/corpus_rel
export SCRM_REPO=$PWD
export SBATCH_PARTITION=<partition>
export SBATCH_ACCOUNT=<account>
export PYTHONPATH=model:eval:target/py
$SCRM_PY -m scrm_eval.registry --recipe armS96-c3k-sigreg-lam002-s20260903
sbatch model/jobs/arm_ablation.sbatch armS96-c3k-sigreg-lam002-s20260903
steps.explanation: REPRODUCE.md's hand path for the reported flagship, armS96-c3k-sigreg-lam002-s20260903 (seed 20260903). The registry command prints the recipe the launcher will use (the four pretraining corpora, seed 20260903, 8947 steps); the launcher writes $SCRM_PROJ/runs/<run>/latest.pt. SCRM_CORPUS_ROOT must be set because every launcher defaults to $SCRM_PROJ/corpus and arm_ablation.sbatch refuses against it. The README instead gives a direct python -m scrm_model.train command that reads $SCRM_PROJ/corpus/... and writes runs/armS96-c3k-sigreg-lam002; REPRODUCE.md gives that name to the seed-floor run (seed 20260817), while the README says train.py's defaults, including --seed, are the flagship's. The saved files do not settle which seed that README command would produce, so this step follows REPRODUCE.md.
